body.statement: For every \(d\le c_{\epsilon}n\log(en)\), there exist priors \(\Pi_0,\Pi_1\) supported on the same class \(\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M}\) and sets \(\mathcal T_0,\mathcal T_1\) such that \(\Delta(\mathcal T_0,\mathcal T_1)\gtrsim_{\epsilon,\alpha}r_{n,d,M}\) and \(\|\mathbb Q_0-\mathbb Q_1\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\le(1-2\alpha)/2\). The rare-cell component starts from the control-arm-zero embedding in \(prop:zeng-one-arm-to-ate-reduction\), then constructs ATE-separated prior supports and verifies prior-predictive total-variation control directly; separate root-\(n\) and saturation priors complete the range. The resulting confidence-length bound \(\mathsf W^*_{n,d,\epsilon,M,\alpha}\gtrsim_{\epsilon,\alpha}r_{n,d,M}\) follows through \(lem:coverage-testing-inequality\), not by taking the square root of the published mean-squared-error bound.
body.justification: This certifies the full confidence-width lower frontier in the identical raw conditional fourth-central-moment class used by the interval.
body.gap: ZengBalakrishnanHanKennedy2024, Theorem 2 and Appendix C.5, lower-bound squared-error risk for the one-arm functional \(\psi_1\). Even after the explicit control-arm-zero reduction transfers that source experiment to ATE point estimation, the published result does not place separated ATE sets inside two same-class priors or invoke uniform coverage to lower-bound expected interval length.
body.consumer: The minimax optimality certificate for the robust interval and a diagnostic showing why shorter 401(k) intervals cannot be uniformly honest without added structure.
